todoai.label: TODOforAI
todoai.capabilities: Delegate work to another TODO: create/list/inspect/update TODOs (real, visible, resumable tasks with their own agent & chat), show files/URLs in the chat (`show list [--project]` enumerates show/card instances), run templates & workflows, platform API access
todoai.description: Manage the user's OWN TODOforAI tasks — NOT code `// TODO` comments. Legacy aliases: `todoforai-cli`, `todoai`. THIS is the tool for delegating/spinning off work: `tfa-cli "prompt"` creates a real TODO the user can see, follow and resume, with its own agent and chat (`-n` run to completion, `--no-watch` fire-and-forget, `--project/--agent/--model` to steer, `--resume <id>`/`-c` to continue, `addmessage <id> "text"` to talk to it). Also: `list` (`--status open`), `--inspect <id>[:<msg-id>]` to read a TODO's chat (read-only), `status`/`delete`, `--template` for registry workflows. Surface a result INTO the chat: `show <file|-> [todo-id]` renders by mimetype (`-` reads stdin), `show --card <name>` renders through a project renderer card, `show list [--project]` enumerates instances (ref/title/card/mime), `open <url> [todo-id]` embeds a live preview; `--title`/`--alias <name>` — re-using an alias UPDATES that block in place instead of appending.

anydoc.capabilities: Convert documents to clean Markdown: doc, docx, pptx, xlsx, odt, ods, odp, rtf, epub, csv. Fully local, no API key.
anydoc.description: Convert office/rich documents to GitHub-Flavored Markdown, entirely local (MIT, no API key, no network). `anydoc report.docx` prints Markdown to stdout; `anydoc slides.pptx -o slides.md` writes a file; `anydoc - --format csv < data.csv` reads stdin. Format is auto-detected from content. Prefer this over raw XML extraction when you need to READ the text of docx/pptx/xlsx/odt/rtf/epub/csv. Not for editing (one-way) and not for scanned/image-only PDFs (needs OCR).

agent-browser.label: Browser
agent-browser.capabilities: Headless browser automation, web scraping, accessibility tree snapshots, screenshots, PDF generation
agent-browser.description: Browser automation over CDP (`open`/`snapshot`/`click`/`type`/`fill`/`read`/`screenshot`/`eval`). If a live browser to drive is listed right below this entry (a `→ Live browser to drive:` line with a connect URL), prefer it over a proxy. Just `connect '<url>'` — a changed connect URL is detected and reattached automatically. After connecting, verify it took (`snapshot` or read the URL); if it hangs or looks empty, `close` (clears your session only) and reconnect once. Never `close --all` even though `--help` offers it — it kills every session on the machine, including other agents'. When several agents share one real browser, open your own tab (`tab new`) and `tab <id>` back to it before each command — the remote browser's active tab is shared. Fallback when no connect URL is listed: on the cloud use browser-manager-cli; on a PC with a display, launch your own Chrome on `--remote-debugging-port=9222` and attach with `--cdp 9222`. Headless only on the cloud / no display.

browser-manager-cli.label: Browser Manager
browser-manager-cli.capabilities: On-demand cloud Chromium sessions exposed as CDP endpoints for agent-browser; create/list/get/delete, hibernate/restore, per-session proxy (stealth Chromium).
browser-manager-cli.description: Spawns cloud Chromium sessions, each exposed as a CDP WebSocket for agent-browser to drive. `create` prints one line ending in a cdpUrl — pass it straight to `agent-browser connect '<cdpUrl>'` (connect the cdpUrl, not the Chrome debug port). `list`/`get <id>`, `delete <id>`/`delete-all`, `hibernate`/`restore`. Sessions run stealth Chromium that reads as a real desktop browser. For sites that block datacenter IPs, route through a proxy: `create --proxy socks5://host:port [--proxy-user U --proxy-pass P]`. Use this on the cloud VM instead of launching a local browser.

todoforai-browser.label: Browser (Extension)
todoforai-browser.capabilities: Browser automation via extension (non-headless), web scraping, accessibility tree snapshots, screenshots, PDF generation

tfa-explore.label: Explore
tfa-explore.capabilities: Read-only sub-agent that maps a codebase and answers where/how/what questions as a hidden TODO. Options: --repo, --tools read,grep,list,bash,webfetch, -m/--model, -p/--project.
tfa-explore.description: Explore a codebase in a separate sub-agent so the file reads and greps never touch your own context — you get back only the answer. `tfa-explore "where is auth handled?"` runs read-only in the repo (`--repo <path>`, default cwd; the path must be in an authorized workspace) and streams the result to stdout. The TODO it creates is hidden from the dashboard. Prefer it over manual multi-file searching for any non-trivial "where/how/what is" question.

tfa-review.label: Review
tfa-review.capabilities: Sub-agent code review of a git diff as a hidden TODO. Options: --repo, --against <ref|WORKING>, --tools read,grep,list,bash,webfetch, -m/--model, -p/--project.
tfa-review.description: Review a git diff in a separate sub-agent, so inspecting the diff and the surrounding files costs none of your own context. `tfa-review "<goal>"` diffs the repo (`--repo <path>`, default cwd) against `--against <ref>` (default `WORKING` = uncommitted) and streams findings, simplifications and issues to stdout. The TODO it creates is hidden from the dashboard. Run it before calling a non-trivial change done.

tfa-summary.label: Summary
tfa-summary.capabilities: Summarize files or piped stdin in a sub-agent as a hidden TODO. Options: -f/--file (repeatable), trailing focus text, -m/--model, -p/--project.
tfa-summary.description: Summarize long input in a separate sub-agent so the raw text never enters your own context: `cat big.log | tfa-summary "what failed?"` or `tfa-summary -f a.md -f b.md "focus"`. Files come from `-f/--file` (repeatable) or trailing paths, the last bare argument is the focus. Streams the summary to stdout; the TODO it creates is hidden from the dashboard.

tfa-handoff.label: Handoff
tfa-handoff.capabilities: Compact a conversation into a handoff document as a hidden TODO; pipe filter for `tfa-cli --inspect … | tfa-handoff … | tfa-cli`
tfa-handoff.description: Compact a conversation into a handoff document for a fresh agent.

tfa-wait.label: Wait
tfa-wait.capabilities: Wait for a boolean expression of triggers; result returns as a message here. Leaves joined by && (all) || (any): `3h` duration, `9:00` clock, `weekdays@9:00` day@time, ISO date, or a `word` webhook (minted URL printed). `--repeat` re-arms, `--until <dur>` caps lifetime, message uses `{{payload.x}}`. Turn ANY command into events: `<cmd> | tfa-wait pipe <name>` (each stdout line → event; JSON line = payload; `--min-gap` flood-guards; cancel stops it). `list`/`cancel`/`emit`. e.g. `tfa-wait 'deploy && tests || 1h' "ship: {{payload.status}}"`, `while true; do check-jsonl; sleep 120; done | tfa-wait pipe signals`.
tfa-wait.description: Schedule wake-ups and wait for events — time (`3h`, `daily@9:00`), webhooks, or `<cmd> | tfa-wait pipe <name>` to turn any command's stdout lines into events; results return into the conversation. Cancelling the wait stops its pipe.

tfa-vault.label: Vault
tfa-vault.capabilities: The user's dedicated password manager and secret store — zero-config TODOforAI KV vault. Commands: put/get/patch/list/rm.
tfa-vault.description: The user's own encrypted secret vault; reading and using its secrets is the intended workflow. READ: when a task needs a secret the user owns (API key, token, password, account), `tfa-vault list` to find it and `tfa-vault get <path>` to fetch it, then use the value (call the API, log in) — don't ask the user for what the vault already holds; treat values as sensitive (pass into commands/env, don't echo). WRITE (do this proactively, unasked): whenever a new secret appears in the conversation — pasted, generated, or handed over by a CLI/login — save it: `get`/`list` first (skip if the same value is already stored), `put <path> field=value` if missing, `patch <path>` to add fields without clobbering, overwrite on rotation. Use namespaced paths (`accounts/<svc>`, `api/<svc>`, `cards/<name>`, `secrets/<name>`).

tfa-memory.label: Memory
tfa-memory.capabilities: The user's persistent memory store — addressable text rows (source/ref) with full-text and semantic search, plus every message of every past TODO federated read-only under the `todo` source. Commands: add/search/ls/get/rm/sources.
tfa-memory.description: The user's long-term memory: notes, procedures, docs, learned facts — addressed as source/ref (e.g. deploy-notes/rollback) — AND every message of every past TODO, searchable read-only under the `todo` source (`todo/<todoId>:<messageId>`), live from the backend message index with nothing separate to sync. READ: before re-deriving anything the user likely already knows or you discussed before, `tfa-memory search "<topic>"` — it covers saved rows and past TODO messages in one shot (add --semantic for meaning-based recall, `--source todo` for past TODO messages only, `--todo <id>` to narrow to one TODO), then `tfa-memory get <source/ref>` for full content. WRITE (do this proactively): when durable knowledge appears in the conversation — a procedure, decision, config fact, preference — save it with `tfa-memory add <source>/<ref> "text"` (re-adding the same address updates in place; identical content is skipped). Use short factual source names (deploy-notes, acme, preferences). `todo` is read-only — you cannot write or delete there. `tfa-memory sources` lists what exists.

todoregistry-cli.label: TODO Registry
todoregistry-cli.capabilities: Browse the public TODO registry (200+ proven business-growth task templates) and create new ones: search/list/get/categories, create.
todoregistry-cli.description: TODO Registry CLI — browse and create proven, reusable business-growth task templates (SEO, email, CRM, ads, social, monitoring, …). `search <query>` / `get <id>` / `list [category]` / `categories` browse the registry. `create --name ... --description ... --body @prompt.md` prints a new template id. To surface a template as a reviewable recommendation card, don’t create a todo directly — use `tfa-cli recommend --template <id> --project <projectId>`; the user accepts it to start a real todo.

tfa-surface.label: Surface
tfa-surface.capabilities: See and drive what is shown in the user's live TODOFORAI UI: `describe` (open todos, focus, panels, embedded-browser CDP URL, on-screen show/card instances), `card add|list|get|rm` (project renderer cards, headless), todo open/focus/close, panel open/close, render markdown into surfaces, get/set controls. UI verbs require an open tab/app; card CRUD does not.
tfa-surface.description: The user's live UI, addressable from the shell (CDP mental model: frontend → todo → panel surface). Target = $TODOFORAI_FRONTEND_ID (override per call: `TODOFORAI_FRONTEND_ID=<id> tfa-surface ...`). DISCOVER: `tfa-surface describe` — what's open (todos, focus, panel surfaces, sidebar, on-screen show/card instances) plus the embedded browser's CDP URL to drive with `agent-browser connect`; `--json` for scripts. CARDS: `card add|list|get|rm <name>` — project-scoped HTML renderer definitions (headless, no frontend needed). VIEWS: `todo open <todoId> [--popout]` / `todo focus|close <todoId>`; `panel open changes|preview|browser|terminal [--todo <id>] [--url <url>]` / `panel close`. CONTENT: EVENTS go in the chat stream; STATE the user should keep visible (plans, reports, live status) goes on a surface: `show chat.panel <todoId> "...markdown..."` (stdin for long content, re-show updates the SAME panel), `clear` removes it; `set todo.status <todoId> '"DONE"'` (permission-gated), `set block.focus <blockId>`. Exit 2 = no frontend id / tab not connected.

wordpress-api.description: WordPress REST API CLI. `wordpress-api auth --site https://example.com --user <user> --password '<application password>'` (application password, not the login password). Reading published content needs no auth. `posts list|get|create|update|delete`, `pages`, `media`, `categories`. `posts create` saves a draft unless --status publish. On Elementor/JetEngine sites content.rendered comes back empty — fetch the post's public URL for the body.

facebook-pages-api.label: Facebook Pages
facebook-pages-api.capabilities: Post to a Facebook Page (published, unpublished or scheduled), read/reply/hide/delete comments, page and post insights, Page inbox, photo posting — official Meta Graph API.
facebook-pages-api.description: Facebook Pages CLI over the official Meta Graph API v21.0. `facebook-pages-api auth --page-id <id> --page-token <token>` (page token from GET /me/accounts; env FB_PAGE_ID / FB_PAGE_TOKEN). `feed list|get|create|delete`, `comments list|get|reply|hide|delete`, `insights page|post`, `conversations list|get`, `media create`. Writes are live — use `feed create --published false` for tests. `comments reply` posts publicly and immediately, so have a human approve the text. Many classic insights metrics (page_impressions, page_fans, post_impressions) were retired and now error; follower totals come from `whoami --fields followers_count,fan_count`. `conversations` needs the pages_messaging permission.

ews-api.label: Exchange (EWS)

ews-api.description: On-premise Microsoft Exchange CLI over EWS (Exchange Web Services), for servers with no Microsoft 365 tenant — use outlook-api for cloud mailboxes. `ews-api auth --email user@corp.hu --username 'DOMAIN\\user' --password ... --server mail.corp.hu` (NTLM; always pass --server, autodiscover is off). `list`, `search <query>`, `read <id>`, `draft`, `reply <id>`. draft/reply save to Drafts by default and only send with --send, so a human approves in Outlook.

outlook-api.label: Outlook (Graph)
outlook-api.capabilities: List/search/read Outlook/Hotmail mail, download attachments, create drafts/replies and send over Microsoft Graph.
outlook-api.description: Outlook / Hotmail / Microsoft 365 mail CLI over Microsoft Graph (cloud mailboxes — use ews-api for on-prem Exchange). `outlook-api auth` is a device-code flow with no Azure app registration; personal accounts use --tenant consumers (default), work/school --tenant organizations. list/search/read/attachments are read-only; `draft` and `reply` save to Drafts by default and only send with --send, so a human approves in Outlook; `send <draftId>` sends an existing draft. Raw JSON out; `get` is a raw Graph GET passthrough.

neonctl.statusCmd: test -f ~/.config/neon/credentials.json && neonctl me --output json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"email"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | grep -m1 .
neonctl.capabilities: Serverless Postgres: projects, branches, databases, roles, connection strings
neonctl.description: Manage Neon Postgres branches and run SQL: `neonctl projects list`, `neonctl branches create`, `neonctl connection-string`. Aliased as `neon`.

m365.label: Microsoft 365
m365.statusCmd: m365 status --output text 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | grep -vi 'logged out' | grep -m1 .
m365.capabilities: Outlook mail & calendar, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Entra ID users and groups
m365.description: Microsoft 365 from the shell: `m365 outlook message list`, `m365 teams team list`, `m365 spo site list`. Device-code login; add `--output json` for parseable output.

hubspot.label: HubSpot
hubspot.capabilities: CRM objects, contacts & deals, CMS themes, serverless functions, HubDB
hubspot.description: Invoked as `hs`. `hs api <endpoint>` makes authenticated calls to any HubSpot API (contacts, deals, companies) — prefer it over raw curl.

posthog-cli.label: PostHog
posthog-cli.capabilities: Product analytics queries, error tracking, source maps, releases, feature flags
posthog-cli.description: Official PostHog CLI. `posthog-cli api tools` lists the agent-first API tool catalog, `posthog-cli api call <tool> '<json>'` runs one (SQL queries, insights, flags). Also uploads sourcemaps/dSYM. Env alternative: POSTHOG_CLI_API_KEY + POSTHOG_CLI_PROJECT_ID.

canva.label: Canva
canva.capabilities: Canva app development: scaffold, preview, deploy apps; Canva Developer MCP server
canva.description: Official Canva CLI — app-development focused: `canva apps create/list/preview`. `canva mcp` starts the Canva Developer MCP server. For design/export automation use the Canva Connect REST API.

webflow.label: Webflow
webflow.capabilities: Sites, CMS collections & items, forms, assets, custom code
webflow.description: Manage Webflow sites from the shell: `webflow sites list`, `webflow cms ...`, `webflow assets ...`. Add `--skip-update-check` in scripts.

readwise.label: Readwise
readwise.statusCmd: readwise whoami >/dev/null 2>&1 && readwise whoami 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -m1 .
readwise.capabilities: Reader documents & highlights: search (incl. vector), save, tag, export, organize
readwise.description: Official Readwise/Reader CLI. `readwise search <query>`, `readwise list`, `readwise save <url>`; supports JSON output for piping and a read-only mode for agents. Token login for CI: `readwise login-with-token <token>` (get one at readwise.io/access_token).

mapps.label: monday.com
mapps.capabilities: monday-code apps: scaffold, deploy, logs, env vars, storage, scheduler
mapps.description: Invoked as `mapps` — app development and monday-code deployments only; `mapps init -t <token>` stores a monday.com API token in ~/.mappsrc. To read/write board DATA use the monday.com GraphQL API (api.monday.com/v2) with that same token.

exa-cli.label: Exa Search
exa-cli.capabilities: Neural web search, page contents, find-similar, grounded answers — built for agents
exa-cli.description: Invoked as `exa`. `exa search <query>`, `exa answer <question>`, `exa contents <url>`, `exa find-similar <url>` — JSON by default. Needs EXA_API_KEY in the environment (get one at dashboard.exa.ai); store it in the vault.

mobbin.label: Mobbin
mobbin.statusCmd: mobbin auth print-cookie 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '[A-Za-z0-9]' && echo authenticated
mobbin.capabilities: Search real-world mobile & web UI patterns, screens and flows for design reference
mobbin.description: Unofficial CLI over Mobbin's undocumented web endpoints. `mobbin search --query "login" --platform ios`. Auth reuses browser cookies: log into mobbin.com in Chrome, then `mobbin auth save-cookie`.
